note: better_normalizers replaces three core HAL normalizers (registered via BetterNormalizersServiceProvider::alter, not config) and only affects the hal_json format. FileEntityNormalizer adds a base64 'data' property of the file contents on normalize and writes the bytes back on denormalize; FileItemNormalizer keeps file-field description/display; MenuLinkContentNormalizer embeds a menu link's target/parent entity. No config, routes, permissions, Drush or UI. Node creation is unavailable on this shared test site (a broken content-moderation stack), so medium/hard cases are grounded in File entities only: introspection serializes a known File entity created by setup; execution normalizes a File entity to hal_json (verify: base64 contents embedded) and denormalizes a HAL document back into a reconstructed file on disk (verify: bytes restored).

evals.prompt: What does the better_normalizers Drupal module change, and which serialization format does it affect?
evals.expected_output: It replaces three core HAL normalizers (for the hal_json format only): File entities (embed base64 contents), file field items (keep description/display), and menu_link_content (embed the linked/parent entity). It requires the hal module and has no config/UI.

evals.prompt: When better_normalizers serializes a File entity to hal_json, what extra does it include compared to core, and how can the file be recreated from that output?
evals.expected_output: Its FileEntityNormalizer adds a 'data' property containing the base64-encoded file contents on normalize; on denormalize it base64-decodes that and writes the bytes back to disk, so the file is recreated from the HAL JSON alone.

evals.prompt: How does better_normalizers improve HAL serialization of menu_link_content links, and which class handles it?
evals.expected_output: MenuLinkContentNormalizer embeds the entity a menu link points at (pseudo-field menu_link_content_target_entity, adding target_uuid) and the parent menu link, and resolves those back to ids/UUIDs on denormalize. It is only registered when menu_link_content is enabled.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a File entity named bnrm-eval-marker.txt. Using the site's serializer, serialize it to the hal_json format and state which JSON property carries the file's actual contents.
evals.expected_output: The hal_json output includes a top-level 'data' property (e.g. "data":[{"value":"<base64>"}]) holding the base64-encoded file contents, added by better_normalizers' FileEntityNormalizer.

evals.prompt: better_normalizers is enabled on this site. Which core HAL normalizer does it override for File entities, and what does that override add to the serialized output? (A File entity bnrm-eval-marker.txt exists that you can serialize to check.)
evals.expected_output: It overrides core's HAL file-entity normalizer with FileEntityNormalizer (service serializer.normalizer.entity.file_entity, priority 30), which adds the base64-encoded file contents under the 'data' property.

evals.prompt: This site has a File entity whose filename is bnrm-eval-spec.txt. Using the site's serializer, normalize that File entity to the hal_json format (the format better_normalizers enhances) and write the resulting JSON to the file /tmp/bnrm-eval/file-out.json. The output must embed the file's contents.
evals.expected_output: /tmp/bnrm-eval/file-out.json contains the hal_json for the file including a 'data' property whose base64 value decodes to the file's contents (BNRM-EVAL-CONTENT-42) -- produced by \Drupal::service('serializer')->serialize($file, 'hal_json'). This only appears because better_normalizers' FileEntityNormalizer is active.

evals.prompt: A HAL JSON document describing a File entity (with its contents embedded) is saved at /tmp/bnrm-eval/in.json. Using the site's serializer, deserialize/denormalize it back into a File entity and save it, so the file is written to disk. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Deserializing /tmp/bnrm-eval/in.json to Drupal\file\Entity\File in hal_json and saving it re-creates public://bnrm_eval/restore.txt on disk with its original bytes (RESTORE-BYTES-88), because better_normalizers' FileEntityNormalizer::denormalize base64-decodes the 'data' property and writes the file.
